To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cross sections for the production of heavy quarks in leptoproduction at high energies are dominated by the photon‐gluonsub(1) channel, that the cross sections are very large, and that they are sensitive to the gluon distribution in the photon.

(1) the photon‐gluo n fusion model for heavy quark production, which is based on perturbative QCD, is consistent with all available experimental results; (2) this consistency is not surprising, as the model predicts that the heavy quark production cross section is proportional to the square of the gluon distribution function;
the cross section for the photon‐gluo fusion model is σ = (1.3±0.2) mb at √ s = 30 GeV, (1.5±0.2 mb at √ s= 100 GeV, and that the next order calculation will increase the cross section by 20%–40%.

the photon‐gluo fusion model of heavy‐quark production is the best available model.

the present status of the photon‐gluo fusion model is that it is a viable candidate for the description of the heavy quark production mechanism, but that the model is still in need of experimental verification.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photon‐gluons fusion model is a very good description of heavy quark leptoproduction.
we find the photon‐gluonic model of heavy quarks production to be a very promising approach, but one in need of further theoretical development and experimental tests.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the photon‐gluo fusion model of heavy‐quark production is not a good approximation to the full calculation, even for the lowest order.

the photon‐gluonic model is a very good approximation for the heavy quark production cross section, but that it is not a good approximation for the angular distribution of the heavy quark in the photon rest frame.
